statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail eases to 6% in the low band roughly six and a half hours into the Globex session, with NQ rotating off its session high for a second time inside an unchanged 226-point range.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow evidence-based danger window is flagged over 13:00-15:00 UTC, the window containing Monday's US cash open, where an opening-auction imbalance can extend before it retraces. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ rotates off its high again at 30,083.75 (+0.56%) with the 226-point range intact; live WTI $94.08 and Brent $97.61 hold their declines and Hang Seng adds 0.57% with Tokyo shut - Tail eases to 6%, Stress 31%
body:
Roughly six and a half hours into the Globex session the price path has done the same thing twice, and that repetition is the substantive change this hour. NQ prints 30,083.75 on Yahoo, up 166.50 points (+0.56%) against the 29,917.25 Friday settle, timestamped 00:15 EDT (04:15 UTC). Investing.com shows 30,083.75 at 00:16 - the two feeds agree to the tick, not merely to within a point or two. The observed session range is unchanged at 29,904.50-30,130.50, so no new high and no new low has been set in the last hour. Price now sits 46.75 points below the session high, against 34 points an hour ago and 51 points the hour before that. The index has therefore pulled back from the high, recovered part of the way, and pulled back again, all without extending the range. That is a second completed rotation rather than a single ambiguous one, and repeated mean reversion inside a fixed 0.75% envelope is the specific behaviour this Tail measure is defined against. Tail eases to 6% accordingly. It does not fall further because the range is still young and the session's dominant liquidity has not yet arrived.

Investing.com reports its day range as 30,019.25-30,130.50 against Yahoo's 29,904.50-30,130.50. The difference is a session-boundary convention rather than a data conflict: the two feeds agree on the high to the tick and disagree only on how far back the day is measured. The Globex-session range used here is the wider one.

The energy complex has held the move that was established an hour ago rather than retracing it. Yahoo's front-month CL=F prints $94.08, down 2.08%, inside a $93.58-$97.03 session range; Brent on BZ=F prints $97.61, down 1.69%, inside $96.98-$100.26. Both are stamped 00:15 EDT. Crude sitting four dollars below where earlier runs in this cycle carried it, and Brent consolidating below $100 rather than snapping back through it, is a disinflationary and risk-positive alignment. Trading Economics still shows the older, higher levels, and the same page dates its 10-year yield observation to 18 September, so it continues to be treated as a lagging reference rather than a live quote.

The diplomatic branch behind that move was updated at 03:28 UTC. Gulf News reports Trump telling Fox News he would 'probably be open' to meeting Iranian President Pezeshkian at the UN General Assembly, which runs 22-28 September, while describing himself as in 'deciding mode' between continued economic pressure, military action and a negotiated deal. Iran has conveyed seven conditions through mediators, including an end to the war, release of frozen assets and lifting of the naval blockade. Trump is separately scheduled to meet Gulf leaders on the conflict. A meeting being possible is not a meeting being agreed, and the verified escalation reports from the weekend - an intercepted Houthi ballistic-missile attempt on Riyadh, the first on the Saudi capital in this phase, plus thwarted attempts at Yanbu, Taif, Baysh and Farasan - have not been withdrawn. A crude complex that keeps selling into those headlines is pricing the diplomatic branch. The escalation is therefore carried as Stress and headline-gap risk, not as an established Tail path.

Asian cash trade gives the first genuine cross-asset confirmation available in this cycle. Hang Seng trades 24,891.58, up 140.80 points (+0.57%), at 12:05 Hong Kong time. That is almost exactly the NQ move and it is constructive without being extended. Tokyo is closed for Respect for the Aged Day, so the regional complex is running without its largest cash market; thinner books make individual prints erratic without making them directional, and the hours until the European open should be read with that in mind.

The rate backdrop is unchanged and remains the heaviest standing weight. The FOMC raised rates 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September, its first hike in three years, and signalled at least one more this year. The 10-year sits at 5.00% and the 2-year at 4.75% as of the 18 September close; the latest H.15 observation, dated 17 September, reads 4.94% and 4.67%. Fed funds futures are reported around 57% for an October hike and close to certain for December. Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is still too high in all aspects of the economy, echoing Chair Warsh, who put August PCE near 3.6%. VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08%, and is static while the cash market is shut. The cash reference remains Friday's NDX close at 29,644.17, up 0.67%, set in a tape where the S&P 500 added 0.17% and the Dow shed 0.18% - split internals rather than aligned ones.

The week's principal catalyst was re-verified this hour from a second independent report. Bessent and Greer met Vice Premier He Lifeng and Li Chenggang in New York on Sunday for roughly eight hours; Bessent called the talks very successful, the Board of Trade mechanism is described as operational, and a working group resumes on Monday. The proposed US-China AI dialogue includes an incident notification mechanism but explicitly excludes advanced-chip export controls, and no progress was announced on critical minerals or the November 10 truce expiry. The Trump-Xi summit is confirmed for 24 September in Washington. A preparatory round that concludes constructively and continues narrows dispersion into that summit rather than widening it. Monday's own calendar is light and was re-verified: Goolsbee at 10:30 UTC, the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30 UTC and bill auctions at 15:30 UTC. The Trading Economics calendar page presents figures in its actual column for releases that have not yet occurred today, so no actual value is published here for them.

The shared Finviz context for this run is the same file as an hour ago - collection status partial, with futures and calendar sections failed - and at roughly four hours old it is well outside the freshness bound. It is treated as stale and not relied upon. Its latest-session breadth showed Technology up 0.84% against Communication Services down 0.74%, consistent with the split internals of Friday's cash close, but that is context, not evidence of current structure. The independent research above stands on its own.

Net: Tail 6%, down one point, because a second completed rotation off the session high inside an unchanged range is repeated mean reversion rather than extension, and no retracement has failed. The mapped state stays EA_ON and green. Stress eases to 31% as crude holds its four-dollar decline, Brent consolidates below $100 and Asian cash equities confirm constructively, against an unchanged 5.00% 10-year and a Fed that has just resumed hiking. Confidence rises to 80% on two futures feeds agreeing to the tick at a 04:15 UTC stamp, live oil and Brent futures, a live Asian cash index for cross-asset confirmation, a re-verified seven-day US calendar, and three independently fetched reports including one updated within the last hour; it is discounted for the absence of live US cash-market breadth and for Finviz context that is both partial and stale.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available and describe an unbroken low-Tail regime spanning Sunday 20 September and the Globex reopen into Monday. Tail held between 4% and 9% in every hour, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout. It sat at 4-5% through the weekend halt, rose with the reopen as the first live price path formed, peaked at 9% in the 01:00 UTC slot, then eased to 7% for two consecutive hours as that extension unwound. Stress drifted from 25% early on 20 September into a 30-35% band as the post-hike rate backdrop and the then-elevated oil complex accumulated, easing to 32% in the final hour. Confidence ranged from 70% to 79%, dipping in the deepest part of the halt when no live price path existed and recovering once futures reopened and independent feeds could be cross-checked. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours. The present assessment lowers Tail to 6%, the first decline since the reopen.
outlookSummary: The cycle covers the remainder of the Asian session, the European session, the Monday US cash session through the 20:00 UTC close, the CME maintenance halt and the Tuesday Globex reopen. Tail is projected to stay inside the low band in all 24 hours, so the mapped policy state remains EA_ON throughout. The projected peak is 12% in the hour containing the 13:30 UTC US cash open, followed by 11% in the hour after it, which is why the flagged danger window spans 13:00-15:00 UTC; secondary 10% readings fall on the 12:30 UTC Chicago Fed release hour and power hour into the 20:00 UTC close. The cycle low of 6% covers the current hour and the 21:00-22:00 UTC maintenance halt, when no NQ price path exists and a no-retracement trend is mechanically impossible. Stress is projected between 31% and 36%, held up by a 5.00% 10-year and a Fed that has just resumed hiking, and capped by crude holding a four-dollar decline, Brent below $100 and a constructive US-China preparatory round that continues on Monday. Confidence decays from 80% to 68% across the cycle as the evidence base ages. These are conditional projections: no future price-path structure is treated as already observed, and an upgrade would require observed shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after failed retracements.
